For “Feng coding agents sufficient evidence,” the closest match is “The Missing Complement: State-Conditioned Minimal Sufficient Evidence for Coding Agents.” It argues that coding agents need not just relevant passages, but a set of evidence that is sufficient for what the next decision still lacks, and that sufficiency is not guaranteed by independently scored retrieval results [1]. It formulates state-conditioned minimal sufficient evidence recovery and evaluates it on captured agent states from repositories, crediting only evidence sets that satisfy every annotated evidence requirement of the current decision [1].

This paper differs from retrieval-focused benchmarks that evaluate context recall/precision or upstream file retrieval, since it treats evidence acquisition as set construction and targets what’s missing for the next decision rather than re-ranking “similar” issues [1, 4, 9]. It also differs from broader coding-agent evaluation or digitization studies that may measure evidence recall from traces but do not directly optimize or define minimal sufficient evidence sets [7, 8].
